why: An old-style class is an `@plume` folder whose `plume.m` is a constructor function (`class(s, 'plume')`), named in lower case as such classes usually are. `settle(p)` after `p = plume();` dispatches to its method `@plume/settle.m`, ahead of the function `settle.m` on the path (MATLAB doc 'Function Precedence Order': a method of an argument's class first). The anchor: `settle(q)` after `q = brew();`, a function's value, calls the function `settle.m` (`brew` is no class, so no method of it).
